title: One split per public table everywhere, copies included: the store splits real tables as the lake does, and a copy of a table kept for measuring is never trained on
request: The owner: 'make sure all data must capture and record and store for all 6 models we have', with the plan for more ability (S8) approved; capture correctness first.
spec: Plan 2026-10-25 Part A1 (~/.claude/plans/async-skipping-firefly.md): real-table writers name their table; dclab_core.datasets.split_of sends a public table's group to dclab_core.lake.split_of; a test; the moves reported.
plan: Count the real-table records by the lake's split and the store's.
Ask the other session (the store's author) before changing the split.
Route a public table's group to the lake's split, parsed strictly.
Make the screens' records name their table (a ledger dataset scope).
Report what moves and whether anything leaked.

decisions.decision: The fix is in dclab_core.datasets.split_of, the one function every set builder and the store's shaper call.
decisions.why: One place: the store, the dataset builders and the curriculum read it; a second mapping in the store would drift.

decisions.decision: A public table's group takes the lake's split, not the other way round.
decisions.why: The lake's split is what the real-table exams seal (real_v1, real_v2, the screens); moving it would unseal tables already read once.

decisions.decision: The id is read strictly: the whole group, digits without a leading zero, nothing after them.
decisions.why: The other session's review: 'openml:02' or 'openml-2-copy' must not become table 2's key by accident.

decisions.decision: A ledger dataset scope (ledger.dataset_scope) names the table for every decision inside an engine run; a caller's own dataset wins.
decisions.why: The engine's records carry a random project id; the screens can name the table once around the run instead of in every capture call.
sets/decisions.py recomputes each example's split from its group at build time; the Mac is busy; the next build applies the fix.

decisions.decision: Twins move only to dev, in lake.split_of itself.
decisions.why: Dev is neither trained on nor read as a blind exam: no table becomes train or sealed, so no exam already read changes; and every caller (store, screens, homework, collector) agrees at once.

decisions.decision: The twin signature includes OpenML's qualities, and keeps schema-sharing variants together.
decisions.why: Rows and columns alone held 175 train tables, many synthetic variants; with the qualities 73; the variants left are the same homework for the column students.

change: dclab_core/datasets.py (table_key, split_of routes a public table to lake.split_of), dclab_core 0.112.1 and its CHANGELOG; dclab_rnd/ledger/__init__.py (dataset_scope, _ids carries the dataset); dclab_rnd/real_screen.py (dataset_of, split_for, the run inside the scope); dclab_rnd/store/sets/__init__.py (SPLIT_RULE says it); docs/DATA_CATALOG.md and data_catalog.json (the version); tests/test_public_table_split.py (new). After the review: dclab_core/lake.py (base_split_of, twins, split_of moves a twinned train or sealed table to dev), dclab_core/lake_twins.json (package data) built by dclab_rnd/table_twins.py; real_screen keeps its ledger under ledgers/<did>/ledger where the store reads decisions; the datasets policy text; the report and note corrected.

findings.defect: The store split real tables by a hash of their draft or project (salt dclab-datasets-v1, 20/40) while the lake splits them by openml:<id> (salt dclab-lake-v1, 15/30).
findings.scenario: The store's sets held 545 public tables, all lake-train by id, but 90 of them in its dev split and 96 in its sealed split by the old hash; any new real-table record would have been split by a random project id.
findings.cause: Two split functions for one table: the lake's for its exams, the datasets' for the store; a screen's records carried a random project id and no table.
findings.fix: datasets.split_of sends dataset:openml:<id>, draft:openml-<id> and openml:<id> to lake.split_of; the screens bind the table as the dataset.
findings.test: tests/test_public_table_split.py: one table, three names, the lake's split for ids 1..399 (all three splits seen)

findings.defect: A loose parse could give another group a table's key.
findings.fix: A full match: digits without a leading zero, at most ten, nothing after.

findings.defect: The store's SPLIT_RULE text would have broken every set manifest.
findings.scenario: The longer rule was 230 characters; SetManifest.split_rule allows 200.
findings.cause: A contract limit not read before the text grew.
findings.test: the manifest's contract at the next build; the affected store tests pass

findings.defect: The dev record used a severity the devlog contract refuses.
findings.scenario: 'high': test_devlog and test_datasets errors; make sft-dev would raise.

findings.defect: The screens' decisions never reached the store's decision sets.
findings.scenario: The screen's ledger was opened at ledgers/<did>, so its files were decisions/... and the store classified them as other.
findings.cause: The store reads a workspace's ledger/ folder.
findings.fix: The ledger opened at ledgers/<did>/ledger; a store-level test shapes a lake-sealed screen record and a lake-sealed draft:openml record and finds both sealed.

findings.defect: One table under several OpenML ids sat in different splits: a copy of a table sealed for an exam was in training.
findings.scenario: glass is 41 (real_v1 sealed) and 952 prnn_fglass (store train); iris four times; 25 of DMG-014's 177 sealed tables have a copy in real_v1's train.
findings.cause: The key is the OpenML id, not the table.
findings.fix: Twins found by rows, column names and OpenML qualities (dclab_rnd/table_twins.py, dclab_core/lake_twins.json); lake.split_of gives dev to a train twin of a dev or sealed table and to a sealed table with a twin outside sealed; DMG-014 named as partly not blind (its fail stands).

findings.defect: The changelog and the dev record said the next store build would have trained on 84 lake-dev tables.
findings.scenario: Those ledgers are in an evaluation workspace whose consent keeps them out of training (counts only).
findings.cause: The count read every ledger on disk without its consent.
findings.fix: The text says what was measured.

findings.defect: The datasets manifest described the old split for public tables.
findings.scenario: make datasets on a real-table workspace would say 20/20 by hash.
findings.fix: The policy text names the lake's split for a public table.

measurements.name: what moves
measurements.result: the sets hold 545 public tables, all lake-train by id; with the twins, 40 tables of their train files (9,099 rows) are now dev; 90 store-dev and 96 store-sealed lake-train tables go to train (sealed ones in a new version); DMG-014 was partly not blind (25 of 177 sealed tables have a copy in train)
limits: the ledgers not yet shaped are counted from their files, not from the store

measurements.name: affected tests
measurements.gate: affected tests only (the owner's daytime rule)
measurements.result: 116 tests in 16 files pass (datasets, store sets and shapers, tutor, screens, shadow, collector, curriculum, real homework, first family, lineage, core wheel, the data catalog after make catalog)

outcome: One table, one split, in the lake, the screens and the store, and copies of a table kept for measuring held out of training; the one exam that read copies is named.
lessons: Two hash functions over the same thing are two partitions: when a split matters for an exam, there must be exactly one function that decides it.
Read a contract's limits before growing a text that goes into it.
An id is not a table: public datasets are uploaded again under new ids, so a split by id leaks copies.
risks: Rows already written to a v1 set's sealed file stay sealed (by design): those 106 lake-train tables teach only from the next set version.
